newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone rises in active trading. [CORRECTED 19:12 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Danone rises in active trading. [CORRECTED 19:12 GMT]

text.p: Shares in French foods group Danone rose sharply in robust volume on Tuesday in a market looking for underperformers and companies with scope for restructuring, market sources said.

Market professionals looking for an explanation for the rise cited the appearance of Danone in Morgan Stanley's portfolio of European stocks, replacing Cie Generale des Eaux. But the U.S. broker said its decision dated back to Monday (corrects day), February 28. It set a target of 950 francs per share for Danone.
Danone traded up 3.52 percent at 911 francs at 1458 GMT, while the market was up 1.57 percent.
Generale des Eaux lagged the market, rising 0.88 percent.
Danone has risen since Club Mediterranee replaced chairman Serge Trigano with Philippe Bourguignon, ex-head of Euro Disney and the merger announcement of Worms et Cie and Saint-Louis.

Since the Agnelli group are shareholders in both of these groups as well as Danone, investors think the Italian group wants to improve the profitability of their French investments, market sources said.
